svg.title: The TPA Program Squeeze
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-tpa-program-squeeze; chapter number: 6; title: The TPA Program Squeeze; subtitle: How program work narrows a contractor's pricing control; chart type: funnel; stages: label: Claims Routed Through TPAs; value: 80; display: Upwards of 80% of claims; conversion: Entry point, very few adjusters still work for insurers; detail: The DYOJO host puts the TPA share at upwards of 80% of claims, and Jon Schoen says very few adjusters still work directly for carriers.; label: Carriers Bundled per Program; value: 40; display: 30 to 40 carriers; conversion: Each carrier requires separate approval; detail: Programs such as Contractor Connection bundle 30 to 40 carriers, and the contractor must be approved by each one separately.; label: Markup Surrendered at Entry; value: 20; display: 20% over the standard list; conversion: Preset, discounted list that cannot be changed; detail: Outside programs Jon Schoen marks the standard price list up 20%. Inside a program the list is preset and discounted with no markup.; label: Program Fee Charged; value: 10; display: 5% to 10% of the work; conversion: Fee paid by the contractor to do program work; detail: Schoen reports that TPAs charge the contractor 5 to 10 percent in order to do the work, on top of the preset price list.; label: Drying Capped at 3 Days; value: 3; display: 3-day drying cap; conversion: Cap credited with $20M in claimed savings; detail: Contractor Connection won Nationwide back from Alacrity by capping drying at 3 days and claiming $20M in savings (Jon Schoen).; caption: Program work trades chasing for control, yet David Smith says a program can hand over a $250,000 fire nobody had to chase.; assumptions note: Stage values carry mixed units (percent of claims, carrier count, percent of price, days) and are plotted as reported figures, not conversion rates. The 30 to 40 carrier range is plotted at its upper bound and the 5 to 10% fee at its upper bound.; note: Attributed to Water Damage Restoration Coach Jon Schoen and The DYOJO, including Oregon mitigation owner David Smith. Brian Close counters that guaranteed work is not always profitable.

rect.title: label: Claims Routed Through TPAs; value: 80; display: Upwards of 80% of claims; conversion: Entry point, very few adjusters still work for insurers; detail: The DYOJO host puts the TPA share at upwards of 80% of claims, and Jon Schoen says very few adjusters still work directly for carriers.

label: Carriers Bundled per Program; value: 40; display: 30 to 40 carriers; conversion: Each carrier requires separate approval; detail: Programs such as Contractor Connection bundle 30 to 40 carriers, and the contractor must be approved by each one separately.

label: Markup Surrendered at Entry; value: 20; display: 20% over the standard list; conversion: Preset, discounted list that cannot be changed; detail: Outside programs Jon Schoen marks the standard price list up 20%. Inside a program the list is preset and discounted with no markup.

label: Program Fee Charged; value: 10; display: 5% to 10% of the work; conversion: Fee paid by the contractor to do program work; detail: Schoen reports that TPAs charge the contractor 5 to 10 percent in order to do the work, on top of the preset price list.

label: Drying Capped at 3 Days; value: 3; display: 3-day drying cap; conversion: Cap credited with $20M in claimed savings; detail: Contractor Connection won Nationwide back from Alacrity by capping drying at 3 days and claiming $20M in savings (Jon Schoen).

text.title: Assumptions: Stage values carry mixed units (percent of claims, carrier count, percent of price, days) and are plotted as reported figures, not conversion rates. The 30 to 40 carrier range is plotted at its upper bound and the 5 to 10% fee at its upper bound.

figures, not conversion rates. The 30 to 40 carrier range is plotted at its upper bound and the 5 to 10% fee at its upper bound.
